sources.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas converted to x^0 = c t
sources.locator: Sections 1.1-1.3 pp. 12-28 (simultaneity on operational grids, radar calibration, time dilation, length-contraction road-trip example), Sections 3.5 and 3.7 pp. 60-68 (four-velocity, acceleration, constant proper acceleration, projection operator), Section 3.9.3 pp. 73-74 (local failure of accelerated simultaneity), Section 6.5 pp. 139-140 (optical appearance versus measured length), Sections 7.1-7.3 pp. 147-151 (Rindler coordinates and nonuniform proper acceleration), Section 8.1 pp. 165-169 (rotating synchronization), Section 9.5 pp. 205-211 (congruences, expansion and Born rigidity); printed page numbers as in the PDF text layer

contents.name: Sections 1.1-1.2 pp. 12-21: simultaneity of events on an operational grid and radar calibration of a frame
contents.support: The protocol definition fixes the emission/reflection/reception assignment and the symmetric round-trip convention exactly as the source's radar calibration, with the idealizations and the one-way-convention caveat made explicit.

contents.name: Section 1.2 pp. 20-21: assignment of reflection time (t_send + t_receive)/2 and distance c(t_receive - t_send)/2
contents.support: The theorem proves that for an inertial observer these round-trip assignments reproduce the chart time and rest-frame distance under the adopted ideal-light and ideal-clock postulates.

contents.name: Section 1.3.3 pp. 25-27: time dilation gamma and the clock-comparison setup
contents.support: Recast in the framework's (-+++) convention with x^0 = c t and checked on the exact rational case v = 3c/5.

contents.name: Section 1.3.4 pp. 27-28: length contraction (the road-trip example)
contents.support: Batch 1 of this run deferred this content to sr-observer-measurements; it is realized here through lem-sr-boost-time-length-and-velocity-formulas (ii) and the worked rod example.

contents.name: Section 1.4 p. 31: the one-dimensional boost x' = gamma(x - v t)
contents.support: The boost convention is the batch-2 definition def-lorentz-boost; this page re-derives the coordinate consequences (clock rate, length comparison, simultaneity shift, velocity transformation) in the (-+++) convention.

contents.name: Section 3.5.2 pp. 61-62: constant proper acceleration, hyperbolic world-line t = (1/a) sinh(a tau), x = (1/a) cosh(a tau)
contents.support: The worldline is recomputed with c retained and used as the worked instance of Fermi-Walker transport; its lightlike asymptote and event horizon are not used on this page.

contents.name: Section 3.5.2 pp. 61-62: lightlike asymptote and associated event horizon of the hyperbolic observer
contents.reason: The asymptote, horizon and chart-domain discussion are the explicit subject of the accelerated-observers page, whose design reserves the hyperbolic worldline chart and its horizon.

contents.name: Section 3.7 pp. 66-68: the projection operator onto an observer's rest space and the identity d gamma/dt = gamma^3 a . v
contents.support: The rest metric h, the projection and the kinematic decomposition of this page are the coordinate-free form of the projection-operator calculus; the time-derivative identity is recovered from the decomposition.

contents.name: Section 3.9.3 pp. 73-74: local failure of simultaneity for accelerated observers
contents.support: The rotating example computes the exact rest-space holonomy 15 pi R/(8c) at Omega R = 3c/5 and the nonintegrability of the rest distribution, which is the precise form of the source's observation.

contents.name: Sections 7.1-7.3 pp. 147-151: Rindler chart, its domain and nonuniform proper acceleration
contents.support: The chart map, inverse, pullback metric, unit congruence, acceleration c^2/rho and Born rigidity are all recomputed and verified exactly.

contents.name: Section 8.1 pp. 165-169: rotating synchronization and the nonclosed ring synchronization
contents.support: The rigid-rotation clause of the theorem and the worked ring example carry the rotating-coordinate metric and the nonzero circulation of the rest-space covector.

contents.name: Section 8.1 pp. 165-169: guided-ray Sagnac round-trip delay
contents.reason: The guided-ray Sagnac timing claim is the reserved content of the stable item pthm-sr-guided-ring-sagnac-delay on the accelerated-observers page and is not part of the observer-measurement interface.

contents.name: Section 9.5 pp. 205-211: congruences, expansion and Born rigidity L_u h = 0
contents.support: The definition of Born rigidity, its equivalence to vanishing expansion and the kinematic decomposition are supplied with complete pointwise proofs.

contents.name: Section 9.5 pp. 205-211: Herglotz-Noether classification with an analyticity assumption (p. 209)
contents.support: The source's proof assumes analytic motion; the page proves the smooth local classification from the researched smooth argument (Giulini Section 5.5 with the omitted calculations supplied), so the source is used only as statement-level corroboration.

contents.name: Section 6.5 pp. 139-140: optical appearance of a moving object is not its measured length
contents.support: The scope clause of the theorem separates the simultaneity-slice length measurement from light-travel-time appearance, with no photograph claim.

contents.name: Chapter 2 pp. 43-52: postulates P1-P6 and their asserted equivalence
contents.reason: This page consumes the adopted model postulates scaffolded in batch 1 and adds no new postulate; the source's axiomatization-equivalence claim is not used or asserted here.

contents.name: Chapter 1 pp. 8-16: inertial frame built from rigid rods and synchronized clocks; coordinates of events; time dilation and length contraction
contents.support: Batch 1 of this run deferred the rod-and-clock frame construction to sr-observer-measurements; it is realized here through the radar theorem and the measurement theorem, in the framework's SI coordinates.

contents.name: Chapter 1 closing paragraph of the SR section: applying the boost formulae yields time dilation and length contraction
contents.support: Batch 2 of this run deferred the measurement consequences of the boost to this page; the lemma derives the clock-rate, length-comparison, simultaneity and velocity formulas explicitly.

contents.name: Chapter 1 pp. 26-27: equations (1.96)-(1.99), proper time of a timelike path and four-velocity
contents.support: The proper-time and four-velocity constructions were scaffolded in batch 3 (sr-worldlines-and-clocks); this page uses them through def-sr-proper-time and def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration without re-minting them.

contents.name: Chapter 3 pp. 68-71: variation of the proper-time functional and the geodesic equation
contents.reason: The general fixed-endpoint variational derivation of the geodesic equation is excluded from this flat observer-measurement pair. The earlier worldlines-and-clocks pair supplies proper-time definitions and reparametrization, not geodesic variation; the flat endpoint bound and maximum are actually supplied on sr-proper-time-comparisons by thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum through direct integration. Neither that theorem nor any current observer-measurement claim requires this general variational argument or a later GR supplier.

sources.title: D. Giulini, Algebraic and geometric structures of Special Relativity, arXiv:math-ph/0602018; signature (+---) converted to (-+++)
sources.locator: Section 5.5 'Rigid motion' pp. 41-49: Definition 7 and equation (123) (Born rigidity L_u h = 0), equations (125)-(126), Proposition 14, the kinematic decomposition (134)-(135), Lemma 16 (curvature relation), Theorem 15 part 1, Lemmas 17-18, Theorem 19 part 2, and the Rindler/boost example (127)-(133)

contents.name: Definition 7 and equations (122)-(123): normalized timelike field, h = c^-2 u-flat (x) u-flat - g and Born rigidity L_u h = 0
contents.support: Reformulated in the (-+++) convention as h = eta + n-flat (x) n-flat with eta(n,n) = -1 and L_n h = 0; the scaling identity (125) is used only to fix the normalization.

contents.name: Proposition 14: the motion is rigid iff the shear and expansion vanish, theta = 0
contents.support: Proved as the identity (L_n h)_{ab} = 2 theta_{ab} from the kinematic decomposition.

contents.name: Equations (134)-(135): kinematic decomposition of the velocity one-form into theta, omega and the acceleration term
contents.support: Supplied in the flat model as nabla_a n_b = -n_a a_b + theta_ab + omega_ab with all horizontality and symmetry properties checked.

contents.name: Lemma 16: horizontal projection of the ambient curvature versus the slice curvature, Pi_h R = -R-hat - 3 (id - Pi_wedge) omega (x) omega
contents.support: The source states Lemma 16 without proof; the page proves the flat-space specialization R-bar_ijkl = -3 omega_ij omega_kl explicitly in an adapted coframe, which is the omitted calculation recorded in the source-resolution note.

contents.name: Theorem 15 part 1 (Noether-Herglotz): a rotational rigid motion in Minkowski space must be a Killing motion
contents.support: Proved locally on flow boxes and globally on connected simply connected regions with a positive rescaling, with no analyticity assumption.

contents.name: Lemmas 17-18: Killing iff rigid with exact acceleration one-form; the rotational branch has L_u a-flat = 0
contents.support: The proof reproduces Lemma 17 (a-flat = d log f) and Lemma 18 (a is basic, hence da = 0 in the rotational branch).

contents.name: Theorem 19 part 2: all irrotational rigid motions are orthogonal affine-plane tubular families determined by a timelike curve
contents.support: Proved locally with the implicit-function label and the positive lapse 1 + eta(z'', x - z), replacing the source's global orbit quotient.

contents.name: Example (127)-(133): boost Killing field, hyperbolic flow, Rindler coordinates and acceleration c^2/x_0
contents.support: Converted to the (-+++) convention with x^0 = c t and checked exactly on the wedge.

contents.name: Global construction via the quotient of orbits (Omega simply connected, orbit space a manifold)
contents.support: The page deliberately avoids the global quotient assumption: conclusions are local on flow boxes, and the global rescaling is obtained from the closed 1-form primitive on connected simply connected regions.

contents.name: Ehrenfest-type discussion and the acceleration/size limitation of rigid bodies
contents.reason: The physical rigid-body size restriction and the Bell/breaking discussion belong to the accelerated-observers page, whose design reserves the accelerated congruences and their caveats.

canonical.name: Worked inertial radar round trip with exact null segments and midpoint assignments
canonical.support: Exact evaluations in the inertial chart; the nullity and the radar values are read off from lem-sr-radar-midpoint-for-inertial-observer.

canonical.name: Worked time dilation of a clock moving at 3c/5
canonical.support: Exact proper-time rate 4/5 and four-velocity U = (5c/4, 3c/4, 0, 0) with eta(U,U) = -c^2.

canonical.name: Worked length contraction of a rod of rest length 5 at 3c/5
canonical.support: Exact transition computations at equal x-time and equal x'-time giving the factor 4/5.

canonical.name: Worked velocity transformation: collinear, transverse and null cases
canonical.support: Exact rational values 5/13, 2c/5 and the null limit, verifing subluminality.

canonical.name: Worked Rindler wedge congruence: chart, metric, acceleration and non-coordinate frame
canonical.support: Exact bijection, pullback metric, Christoffel computation a = rho^{-1}partial_rho and the nonzero commutator.

canonical.name: Worked rigid rotation: rest-space holonomy 15 pi R/(8c) and failure of ring synchronization
canonical.support: Exact rational computation at Omega R = 3c/5 with the induced cylinder metric and the nonintegrability of the rest distribution.

canonical.name: Worked Bell-type translated congruence with constant separation but nonzero expansion
canonical.support: Exact expansion theta(s,s) = gamma^3 alpha^2 t/c^3, nonzero exactly when t is nonzero (alpha > 0), while the members labelled xi_1, xi_2 keep constant separation |xi_1 - xi_2|; no elasticity or breaking conclusion is drawn.

canonical.name: Counterexample: a Born-rigid (irrotational) congruence need not be a Killing congruence
canonical.support: Exact local construction with pullback metric -N^2 dlambda^2 + dxi^2 + dy^2 + dzeta^2, N = 1 + lambda xi/L_0^2: the field n = N^{-1} partial_lambda is future unit, Born rigid and irrotational, with acceleration form (k/N) dxi and nonvanishing da-flat = (1/(L_0^2 N^2)) dlambda ^ dxi; a positive Killing rescaling would force d log f = a-flat and hence da-flat = 0, a contradiction. The Rindler congruence is not the counterexample (its rho n = partial_theta is Killing); the rotational branch of the Herglotz-Noether classification is preserved.

canonical.name: Counterexample: simultaneity depends on the observer vector
canonical.support: Exact pairings 0 and 3/4 for the same spacelike displacement against two future unit timelike vectors.

canonical.name: Worked Fermi-Walker transport along uniformly accelerated hyperbolic motion
canonical.support: Exact hyperbolic-function computations verifying both legs of the transported tetrad and the difference from parallel transport.
